title: CEO Interview with Vivek Raghuraman of Mixx Technologies - Semiwiki
gist: Mixx Technologies CEO Vivek Raghuraman argues optical scale-up for AI inference stalls not on performance but on connectors, laser supply, packaging yield and network-OS integration; Mixx's first product, the SxC connector (24,576 fibers per rack unit, 4x MMC-VSFF density), launched at SEMICON Taiwan with volume production targeted through 2027-2028.

insights.claim: According to Mixx's CEO, optical interconnect programs rarely stall on performance; they stall at the connector, the laser supply chain, packaging yield and the network operating system boundary.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Bottlenecks in co-packaged optics adoption are integration and supply-chain problems, pointing value toward connector, laser and packaging suppliers rather than raw-speed innovators.
insights.quote: It is rarely performance. It stalls at the connector, in the laser supply chain, in packaging yield, and at the network operating system boundary.

insights.claim: Hyperscalers have decades of reliability data on copper but very little on optics at production scale, so their questions center on qualification, yield, second sourcing and network-OS impact rather than speed.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Copper-to-optics transition timing will be gated by qualification data and second-source availability, which slows adoption versus hype.
insights.quote: Nobody asks whether optics is fast enough.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Roughly 99 percent of laser power is lost before the light reaches the receiver in current optical links, mostly at the connector and inside the photonics platform, and that loss cascades into electrical noise, forward error correction, power and cost.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Link-budget loss is a hidden cost driver; whoever cuts connector/photonic loss captures power and cost savings at deployment density.
insights.quote: roughly 99 percent of laser power is lost before the light signal hits the receiver
insights.locator: The link budget is the other one

insights.claim: An operator that cannot close the link budget at deployment density cannot deploy optics at all, regardless of demo results.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Demo performance claims in optics are poor predictors of deployment; watch for density-scale link-budget closure.
insights.quote: An operator who cannot close the link budget at deployment density cannot deploy at all, whatever the demo showed.
insights.locator: The link budget is the other one

themes.theme: Inference drives radix and scale-up optics

insights.claim: Mixture-of-experts and agentic inference workloads require every node to reach every other node, making radix (endpoints per node) the key scale-up network metric.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shifts in AI workload mix (MoE, agents) change networking demand toward high-radix all-to-all fabrics.
insights.quote: Mixture-of-experts and agentic workloads need every node to reach every other node, and that comes down to radix
insights.locator: Inference is changing what a scale-up network

insights.claim: Higher radix removes switching layers, and each removed layer eliminates its switches, transceivers and cables, lowering latency, aggregate power and failure points.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: High-radix optics is deflationary for switch/transceiver unit counts per cluster, a second-order risk to vendors of those layers.
insights.quote: Each layer removed takes its switches, transceivers, and cables with it
insights.locator: Inference is changing what a scale-up network

insights.claim: Mixx claims its architecture connects 256 GPUs in one all-to-all domain within the latency and power envelope that copper-first systems reach at eight GPUs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If validated, optical scale-up could massively expand scale-up domain size versus copper, reshaping rack architecture.
insights.quote: our architecture connects 256 GPUs in one all-to-all domain inside the latency and power envelope that copper-first systems reach at eight

insights.claim: A 200T switch brings thousands of fibers out of one chassis, and the front panel now runs out of space before the silicon does.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Faceplate/connector density is becoming the binding constraint on switch scaling, creating demand for high-density connectors.
insights.quote: Today the front panel runs out before the silicon does.

insights.claim: The industry is moving to co-packaged optics incrementally via near-package optics, CPX and similar socketed approaches, each step requiring more optical I/O than existing connectors can carry.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: CPO adoption is a stepwise path, not a single cutover, so intermediate socketed formats and connectors see near-term demand.

insights.claim: Mixx's SxC connector terminates up to 24,576 fibers in a single rack unit, four times the density of MMC-VSFF, described as the densest connector platform qualified for deployment today.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A 4x density jump at the connector layer could make Mixx a gatekeeper in front-panel optical I/O.
insights.quote: The SxC™ Connector terminates up to 24,576 fibers in a single rack unit, four times the density of MMC-VSFF
insights.locator: That is why our first product is a connector.

insights.claim: Mixx showed a 512-radix optical engine at 100 Tbps on 200G lanes at OFC 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals the engine roadmap behind the connector business.
insights.quote: a 512-radix design at 100 Tbps on today’s 200G lanes
insights.locator: That is why our first product is a connector.

insights.claim: Mixx deliberately chose the less glamorous options: DR-based 1310 nm lasers from vendors hyperscalers already qualify, linear interfaces aligned to 200G/400G Optical MSA and CPX MSA, passive fiber attach, and network OS continuity, after watching opposite choices fail at hyperscalers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Qualification-friendly design choices can beat performance-maximal CPO designs in winning hyperscaler sockets.
insights.quote: Each was the less glamorous option.
insights.locator: There is a lot of good engineering

insights.claim: By engineering both the optical engine and connector in one link budget, Mixx claims under 1 dB waveguide-to-fiber loss versus 2.5 to 3 dB in the field, recovering roughly 60 percent of the link budget end to end.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vertical integration of connector plus engine is the claimed source of a large efficiency edge.
insights.quote: SxC™ reaches under 1 dB waveguide-to-fiber against 2.5 to 3 dB in the field
insights.locator: At the connector layer we work

insights.claim: Mixx works alongside US Conec, Corning, Molex and 3M at the connector layer and engages several of them through the Expanded Beam Optics MSA, whose first connector spec is in development.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Incumbent connector suppliers are partners in the EBO standard, indicating where the connector ecosystem is heading.
insights.locator: At the connector layer we work

insights.claim: Optical cable assembly remains largely manual across the industry, and Mixx is automating it with robotic fiber assembly and automated visual inspection.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Manual fiber assembly is a scaling bottleneck and a target for automation investment.
insights.quote: cable assembly is still largely manual across the industry
insights.locator: The rest of the SxC™ family

insights.claim: Mixx closed a $33 million Series A in December 2025 led by ICM's HPQC Fund with TDK Ventures, Systemiq Capital and Ajinomoto Group Ventures, with R&D in San Jose, India and Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Strategic corporate investors (TDK, Ajinomoto) back optical interconnect startups, signaling materials/packaging interest.
insights.locator: We built Mixx to address these four points.

insights.claim: Mixx is sampling with customers this year, targeting engineering-sample qualification in 2027 and volume production through 2027 and 2028.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Revenue from optical scale-up products like this is a 2027-2028 story.
insights.quote: We are sampling with customers this year, with engineering-sample qualification in 2027 and volume production through 2027 and 2028.
insights.locator: At the system level, and earlier

insights.claim: Hyperscalers engage Mixx at the system level with a rack architecture and qualification calendar, typically starting with connector and cabling architecture because that is where the optical transition is decided.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Connector/cabling architecture is the decision point for optics adoption, making it a strategic wedge.
insights.quote: Engagements usually start with the connector and cabling architecture, because that is where the transition is decided
insights.locator: At the system level, and earlier
